facts: The research article was published in Frontiers in Computer Science in 2025.
The survey is titled "Large Language Models Meet NLP."
The authors are from Central South University, Harbin Institute of Technology, University of Hong Kong, Tsinghua University, and University of Illinois at Chicago.
The survey examines the integration of Large Language Models with Natural Language Processing.
This study provides an overview of Large Language Models (LLMs) like ChatGPT in Natural Language Processing.
The authors introduce a unified taxonomy with two paradigms: parameter-frozen and parameter-tuning.
The work summarizes new frontiers and associated challenges in the field of LLMs.
The study aims to offer insights into LLMs' potential and limitations in NLP.
Large language models (LLMs) include GPT-series, PaLM-series, OPT, and LLaMA.
LLMs demonstrate impressive zero-shot performance and emergent abilities.
The paper introduces a new taxonomy of LLMs consisting of two paradigms.
The authors provide curated resources to advance the field of NLP.
The parameter-frozen paradigm includes zero-shot learning and few-shot learning.
Zero-shot learning offers the lowest resource consumption and best out-of-domain generalization.
Full-parameter tuning achieves optimal in-domain performance but requires high resources.
Parameter-efficient tuning matches full-parameter tuning results with fewer resources and improved generalization.
Sentiment Analysis uses instruction tuning for zero-shot capabilities across multilingual texts.
Information Extraction includes Named Entity Recognition, Relation Extraction, and Event Extraction.
Dialogue Understanding encompasses Spoken Language Understanding and Dialogue State Tracking.
Parameter-efficient methods like LoRA are used in full-parameter tuning for opinion mining.
Zero-shot approaches like GPT-3 demonstrate superior performance in Summarization without fine-tuning.
LLMs like CodeT5+, CodeLLama, and Qwen2.5-Coder excel at zero-shot and few-shot learning in Code Generation.
Multilingual instruction-tuning benefits Machine Translation by improving zero-shot performance.
Zero-shot chain-of-thought prompting is used in Mathematical Reasoning tasks.
Multilingual LLMs aim to extend English-centric LLM success to over 7,000 languages.
Multi-modal LLMs require advances in complex reasoning and effective multi-modal interaction mechanisms.
X-of-thought (XoT) enhances logical reasoning through step decomposition and prompt knowledge integration.
Safety in LLMs addresses copyright, hate speech, bias, and psychological concerns through comprehensive safety benchmarks.
The survey on Large Language Models was authored by Libo Qin et al. and published in Frontiers in Computer Science in 2025.
The research documented in the survey spans from 2021 to 2025.
The survey discusses parameter-efficient fine-tuning techniques such as LoRA and prefix-tuning.
The work was supported by funding from the National Natural Science Foundation of China.
